subject: ParcelWave post-incident brief: mitigation timeline, owners, and delivery slate
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@parcelwave.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example
Cc: ParcelWave Infra <infra@parcelwave.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Major latency spike this morning — immediate readout requested

Olga / Grace,

We saw a sustained 4–5x latency spike and a sharp uptick in 500 errors between 08:20–08:48 PDT that impacted about 12% of production requests for our peak routing. This caused a downstream retry storm on our side and ~13k failed customer requests. Our SREs mitigated by shifting traffic away at 08:50 but we need a formal readout and commitment on fixes — our execs want a clear remediation timetable for Monday.

Can you share an initial RCA and a list of concrete owners for each mitigation item? We also need temporary workaround guidance so we can adjust our retry/backoff in-flight if needed.

Thanks,
Dana Li
Head of Infrastructure, ParcelWave

Attachment: incident-log-snippet.txt (log excerpt)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example
To: Dana Li <dana.li@parcelwave.com>, ParcelWave Infra <infra@parcelwave.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example, grace_oconnor@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major latency spike this morning — immediate readout requested

Dana — thanks for flagging and sorry for the impact. We're putting the initial RCA together now. High-level update:

- What happened (prelim): a combination of a KV cache invalidation during a model shard reschedule plus an unusual burst of long-context generation requests which exposed a contention path in our batch scheduler. That caused increased token tail latency and elevated OOM retries for a small subset of inference workers, cascading into higher 5xx rates.
- Mitigation already applied: we rolled a temporary kernel fallback on 08:42 which dropped error rates and we rebalanced traffic away from the affected pool at 08:50.
- Next steps (today): formal RCA and recommended fixes, a short-term runtime patch to avoid the scheduler contention, and a set of operational playbook changes (retry/backoff guidance) for ParcelWave.

I'll attach the draft RCA and a matrix of owners for each action item by EOD. Markus will own the runtime patch; Kimberly will own the SLO reconciliation and monitoring updates; Grace will coordinate customer-facing comms and the mitigation guidance for your infra team.

Can we aim to brief your execs with the slide pack tomorrow morning at 09:00 PT? If that doesn't work, propose a time.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: parcelwave_rca_v1.pdf (draft), mitigation_ticket_list.csv (owner matrix)

From: markus_klein@redwood.example
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example, Dana Li <dana.li@parcelwave.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-11T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major latency spike this morning — initial fix plan and timeline

Folks — quick technical note to clarify owners and ETA for the runtime items: 

- Root cause: the scheduler hot-path holds a mutex during KV cache rehydration when a shard is rescheduled; under high long-seq load that resulted in head-of-line waits. The fallback path reduced parallel kernel usage but did not fully avoid mutex contention.
- Short-term patch (runtime): remove the lock on the hot-path and switch to an atomic CAS for cache-ready flags. I can deliver a gated patch by 2026-10-12 17:00 PT with a canary plan. Owner: markus_klein.
- Medium-term mitigation: introduce per-model async KV rehydration and limit long-seq request concurrency at the front door. Proposal doc linked in Drive. Owner: markus_klein (design) + engineering squad.
- Monitoring: add a prioritized metric for scheduler_wait_ms and an alert at the 99.9th percentile. Owner: kimberly_park.

Note: the patch requires a coordinated deployment window (10–15 min) and a short traffic drain; I'll schedule the canary with Ops and share the runbook.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Olga / Markus,

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A few follow-ups from our ops lead: 
1) Can the canary be scheduled outside our peak (we run 09:00–11:00 PT heavy traffic)? 
2) If we must coordinate a short traffic drain, we need a runbook step that explains safe client-side retry/backoff adjustments so we don't exacerbate the retry storm.
3) Do you expect any change in tokens-per-request billing behavior for the short-term patch?

We can do a 07:00–07:30 PT canary window on 2026-10-13 if that helps.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Director, Platform Operations — ParcelWave

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example
To: Dana Li <dana.li@parcelwave.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@parcelwave.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.example
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example, grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-12T11:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major latency spike this morning — canary timing and customer guidance

Evan — 07:00–07:30 PT on 2026-10-13 works for us for the canary. A few operational notes we will publish: 

- Canary scope: single dedicated shard pool with traffic limited to 3% on-route. Roll forward if metrics for scheduler_wait_ms and 5xx remain flat for three contiguous 60s windows.
- Client guidance (short-term): set exponential backoff starting at 300ms, max retries 2 for idempotent calls; for non-idempotent requests use one retry with jitter and ask ParcelWave to enable their application-side idempotency tokens for the next 24–48h.
- Billing: the patch does not change model semantics or tokenizer behaviour; token billing unchanged. We will flag any anomalous token deltas during the canary.

I'll publish the runbook link and the tentative JIRA tickets (OPS-1872 canary + OPS-1873 monitoring) by EOD.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-14T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: ParcelWave: final RCA, owner slate, and next steps (canary complete)

Dana / Evan —

Attached is the final RCA (parcelwave_rca_v1.pdf) and the action owner slate. Summary and commitments: 

- RCA summary (final): KV cache rehydration during a shard reschedule exposed a scheduler lock under an unusual long-sequence workload; this increased head-of-line scheduling waits and caused a cascade of retries and OOMs for a subset of workers.
- Canary status: canary executed 2026-10-13 07:00–07:25 PT, traffic at 3% on a single shard pool. Observed: scheduler_wait_ms 99.9p reduced by 82% vs baseline; 5xx rate for the pool within normal variance. We saw no token billing delta.
- Owner slate & deadlines:
  * markus_klein — gated runtime patch merged and deployed to canary (done); full rollout to production by 2026-10-16 23:59 PT.
  * kimberly_park — monitoring alert (OPS-1873) and SLO reconciliation completed by 2026-10-15 EOD.
  * grace_oconnor — customer-facing mitigation guide and postmortem slide deck delivered on 2026-10-14 (done).
  * olga_petrov — exec summary and compensation/credit discussion liaison (open) — propose crediting two days of peak usage; will share proposal tomorrow.

Action items open in JIRA: OPS-1872 (canary), OPS-1873 (monitoring), OPS-1874 (frontend concurrency limiter), OPS-1875 (post-incident billing review). Please confirm owners and let me know if ParcelWave needs any additions to the runbook for retries.

Thanks for the coordination. We're treating this as a high-priority program and will provide weekly status updates until all items close.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
